Thanks for the details, Oliver — and sorry for the confusion. I dug into the invite metadata. It looks like my calendar client defaulted to my local timezone when creating the event and the initial invite picked up PST timestamps in the email body; Google usually translates correctly, but forwarded invites can expose the original TZ depending on how the recipient's client parses the ICS.

Actions I took:
- Created a new event and explicitly set the event time zone to Europe/Stockholm (CEST).
- Exported and attached an ICS file (invite.ics) that includes the TZID lines.
- Added a short note in the invite subject: "(Time zone: Europe/Stockholm)" so it displays in clients that ignore the ICS tzid.

I've re-sent the invite — please confirm it shows 17:00 CEST for you and your colleague. If there are still issues we'll send the event as a Zoom link with the time spelled out in the description ("17:00 CEST / 08:00 PDT") to avoid client parsing differences.
